text:
jamie: Quick heads-up — we’re starting the Pulse CI centralization cutover next week (Monday 03/30). Goal is to migrate ad-hoc Jenkins/Actions job fragments into the new Pulse pipeline schema so pipelines are reusable and easier to maintain. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/pulse-ci/docs :wave:

ara: Thanks — timeline? who’s impacted briefly?

jamie: Rollout plan: staggered by team. Week 1: core services (auth, runtime). Week 2: infra & tooling. Week 3: open for opt-ins. Nightly jobs that depend on Jenkins agents will be moved first. Expected small PR changes only.

mike: Will secrets handling change? Our jobs use encrypted Vault tokens in Jenkins.

jamie: Good Q. Pulse supports the Vault plugin and GitHub Secrets. We’ll provide a migration helper that rewrites `secrets:` blocks to `pulse:secrets:`. See snippet in the docs.

sophie: Any breaking changes to runners or parallelism? We rely on heavy matrix jobs.

jamie: Pulse uses dynamic worker pools similar to Buildkite — matrix -> dynamic fan-out. We’ll preserve concurrency hints but you may need to tweak `max_parallel` in the new YAML.

dave: Is there an automated lint/checker so PRs don't accidentally commit old Jenkins stuff?

jamie: Yes — devex will ship a pre-commit hook + a CI validator that fails if legacy `Jenkinsfile` or `jenkins-*` workflows are present. Sample error: `PulseValidatorError: legacy-ci-detected`.

ara: Who do we ping if a migration breaks a production deploy?

mike: @dave has oncall this week but who owns rollbacks?

dave: Oncall will triage. Rollback path: revert PR to previous pipeline in the repo, then trigger `pulse rollback <pipeline-id>` from infra shell. Runbook: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/pulse-rollback.md :warning:

infra-bot: Deploy window scheduled: 2026-03-30T02:00Z — Pulse control-plane v1.2.0 will be promoted to prod. Expected 15m of infra config changes.

jamie: Testing checklist for teams: 1) run `pulse lint` locally 2) run migration helper `./scripts/pulse-migrate --dry-run` 3) open migration PR with `pulse.yml` in `.github/pulse/` 4) request `pulse-migration` label for canary rollout.

mike: Example migrate command?

jamie: ```bash
./scripts/pulse-migrate --repo my-service --branch feature/pulse-migrate --dry-run
# inspect changes, edit if needed, then remove --dry-run to apply.
```

ara: Are we gating this behind any org-level policy? perms?

jamie: Yes — repo admins will need to allow the Pulse Actions runner via an org policy toggle. Security will enable it org-wide after week 2.

sophie: Will the console show cost breakdown per-pipeline? customers ask about cost attribution.

jamie: Yep — Pulse integrates with Costboard and emits per-run cost metadata.

dave: Any impact on Dedicated/Private infra customers?

jamie: For Private, there’s an alternate on-prem pulse-agent image. We won’t change public API calls. Ops will coordinate private deployments; expect a brief maintenance notice for those customers.

mike: Migration PR template please — saves time.
jamie: Template added to docs. Also we’ll host two office-hours sessions: Tue 10am and Thu 4pm (calendar invites out).

ara: Sounds good. I’ll start the dry-run on `auth-service` tomorrow and tag @sophie for review.

sophie: 👍

infra-bot: pulse-control-plane: v1.2.0 promotion started by jamie — job 8821. Logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/8821

jamie: Follow-ups: post any migration blockers here. If you hit permission errors, paste `pulse --debug` output and @dave will take a look. Thanks all :rocket:
